what: All three checklists in chapter 1 are broken: every item's text is squeezed into a 40px column, so it shows one word (or part of a word) per line, and the number badge sits on top of the first word.
evidence: Measured in the browser: every `.checklist li > span` is 40px wide at both widths. The lists are 1871px (P19), 1208px (P33) and 2044px (P36) tall. At 390, P19 reads 'Explain. / Say / who / wrote ...' and P19 item 3 breaks `print("#1 fan of Python")` into 'pri / nt(" / #1 / fan ...'. Cause: assets/ext/py-ch1.css:63-66 still has the old grid checklist (`.checklist li { display:grid; grid-template-columns: 40px minmax(0,1fr) }`). That grid fights the engine rule (comic-widgets.css:229-230), which places the badge absolutely, so the text span lands in the 40px track. Crops: scratchpad/review-visual-py-1-5/c1/1280-034-P19.png, c1/390-034-P19.png, c1/1280-058-P33.png, c1/1280-063-P36.png (deleted after the review; rerun the checker with --shots to see them again).
fix:
Delete the four `.checklist` rules at assets/ext/py-ch1.css:62-66 so the engine's checklist styles apply. The page markup (`
  • …
    • `) already works with the engine version.

what: On phones, the code and terminal blocks in the lamp and ghost panels run 12px past both sides of the panel, so their left borders disappear and the file tabs are cut to 'ools.py' / 'host.py'.
evidence: Automated scan: `pre.code` and `pre.term` stick out 12px on the left and 12px on the right of the section, and the section is clipped by 15px. Crops: c3/390-068-P41.png, c3/390-071-P43.png. Cause: py-ch3.css:125 sets `.creature { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr); justify-items: center }` at phone width, so the unnamed `<div>` holding the file tab, code and terminal is centred at its max-content width, which is wider than the panel. This is the 'ch3 P41/P43 clipping' item listed under [QA] in INTEGRATION_TODO. It is still open.
fix: In the phone media block of assets/ext/py-ch3.css, add `.creature > div { justify-self: stretch; min-width: 0; }`, or give those two divs a class and stretch that class.

what: In the anatomy line of the reader's very first program, the closing parenthesis of `print("Hello, world!")` is cut off at phone width (the line scrolls sideways by 12px), so it looks as if the bracket is missing.
evidence: Automated scan: `p.anat-line` has scrollWidth − clientWidth = 12px at 390. In crop c1/390-019-P10.png the big line ends in a half-cut ')'.
fix: Shrink the anatomy line font on phones in py-ch1.css (for example `@media (max-width:640px){ .anat-line { font-size: 1.5rem } }`), or let its tokens wrap.

what: The walker wraps line 4 as `print("Love,", end="` / `")`, so the space inside `end=" "` (the point of the panel) can't be seen, and the continuation line starts flush left with no indent.
evidence: Crop c1/390-031-P17.png, code card at step 1: line 3 also wraps into three pieces (`print("I",` / `"learned", "print",` / `"today.")`).
fix: In the walker code list on phones, use a hanging indent for wrapped lines (`padding-left: 2ch; text-indent: -2ch`), don't break inside string literals, or let this one card scroll sideways instead of wrapping.

what: In the chapter that teaches 'indentation decides the block', wrapped code lines on phones restart at the left edge. The walker's `print("Hot!` / `Water!")` and the parsons line `print("Brr, it's` / `cold.")` look less indented than the lines around them, which contradicts the lesson.
evidence: Crops: c4/390-028-P15.png (lines 4 and 6 wrap and their second halves sit under the line number), c4/390o-009-EX-ex-x7-parsons.png, c4/390o-027-EX-ex-b5-parsons.png. The same wrapping appears in the parsons and fill comparison tables, which even split words: 'print("Free / zing! Ice' (ex-b4). Engine rule: comic-widgets.css:198 'Exercise lines and tracer code wrap on phones ... (indentation is kept)'. Only the first visual line keeps its indent.
fix: Engine: give wrapped code lines in walker, parsons, spot and comparison cells a hanging indent equal to their leading spaces plus 2ch, for example by wrapping each line's leading whitespace in an inline-block and putting the rest in a span with `padding-left:2ch; text-indent:-2ch`. Also add `word-break: normal; overflow-wrap: anywhere` only as a last resort, so words like 'Freezing' don't split.
